heroData.title: EOR/PEO Services in United States
heroData.subtitle: Navigate complex multi-state employment with co-employment solutions
heroData.description: The US EOR/PEO market helps businesses manage payroll, benefits, and compliance across 50 states with varying regulations. Co-employment models allow companies to share employer responsibilities while maintaining operational control.
heroData.bestFor: Companies hiring remotely across multiple US states without establishing separate entities

steps.title: Employee Information Gathering
steps.description: Collect W-4 (federal withholding), state withholding forms,  I-9 employment eligibility verification, and direct deposit details. Background checks and drug screening if required by industry.

steps.title: Multi-State Compliance Setup
steps.description: Register for state-specific tax withholding, unemployment insurance (SUI), and workers' compensation. Each state has unique registration requirements and timelines ranging from 2-6 weeks.

steps.title: Benefits Enrollment
steps.description: Enroll employees in health insurance (ACA-compliant plans), 401(k) retirement plans, and supplemental benefits. Open enrollment window typically 30 days from hire date.

steps.title: Payroll System Integration
steps.description: Configure pay frequency (weekly, bi-weekly, semi-monthly, monthly), set up time tracking, and establish approval workflows for overtime and paid time off (PTO).

steps.title: EOR Agreement Execution
steps.description: Sign co-employment agreement defining responsibilities. EOR becomes employer of record for tax and legal purposes while client maintains day-to-day management control.

items.title: Permanent Establishment (PE) Risk
items.text: Using an EOR does NOT automatically eliminate PE risk. If employees perform revenue-generating activities central to your business, tax authorities may classify your company as having taxable presence in that jurisdiction.

items.title: Co-Employment Relationship
items.text: In PEO arrangements, your entity remains the legal employer sharing responsibilities. EOR models provide fuller separation - the EOR is the legal employer of record for tax and compliance purposes.

items.title: Multi-State Strategy
items.text: For employees in multiple states, an EOR eliminates the need to register separate entities. Saves $10,000-$25,000 per state in setup costs plus $8,000-$20,000 annually in administration.

items.title: Timeline Advantage
items.text: EOR enables hiring in 5-10 days versus 2-4 months for entity formation. Critical for competitive talent acquisition in tight US labor markets.

steps.title: Review Control Factors
steps.description: IRS Common Law Test: Behavioral Control (do you set hours/methods?), Financial Control (reimbursed expenses?), and Relationship Type. If you control HOW work is done, they are likely an employee (W-2).

steps.title: Determine Exempt Status
steps.description: For W-2s, determine if 'Exempt' (Salaried, no overtime) or 'Non-Exempt' (Hourly, overtime eligible). Tech workers often Exempt, but support roles often Non-Exempt. CA has higher salary thresholds for exemption.

steps.title: Select Engagement Model
steps.description: Hire as W-2 via EOR for full-time, long-term core roles. Use 1099 Contractor status ONLY for project-based, autonomous work to avoid misclassification penalties.

faqs.question: What's the difference between EOR and PEO in the US?
faqs.answer: EOR becomes the legal employer without requiring a US entity. PEO creates co-employment where YOUR existing US entity shares responsibilities. Choose EOR for no-entity expansion; PEO if you have a US company.

faqs.question: How does an EOR handle multi-state compliance?
faqs.answer: The EOR registers in each state where you have employees, managing state-specific tax withholding, unemployment insurance (SUI rates vary 0.5-10%), workers' comp, and labor law posters.

faqs.question: What are typical US EOR costs in 2025?
faqs.answer: Expect $625-$700 per employee monthly, or $200-$1,000+ depending on state complexity. Setup fees run $600-$1,200 per employee. Total employer burden adds 20-30% on top of gross salary.

faqs.question: Can I offer stock options through an EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, typically NQSOs (Non-Qualified Stock Options). ISOs (Incentive Stock Options) generally require a direct employment relationship with the issuing entity, which an EOR structure technically breaks.

faqs.question: Can I transfer employees from EOR to my own entity later?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is a standard 'EOR Conversion' or 'Entity Transfer'. You set up your US entity, then 'hire' the employees from the EOR. Resetting payroll tax accumulators (FICA/SUTA) mid-year can be complex.

items.title: Contract Worker vs Employee Classification
items.description: Use IRS 20-factor test or ABC test (stricter in CA, MA, NJ). Misclassification penalties: back payroll taxes + penalties. EORs can only hire W-2 employees, not 1099 contractors.

items.title: Benefits Benchmarking
items.description: Competitive US benefits: health insurance ($600-$1,200/month employer cost), 401k match (3-6%), PTO (15-25 days), parental leave (6-12 weeks). EORs offer standardized packages or custom options.

steps.title: Time and Attendance Collection
steps.description: Gather approved timesheets, overtime hours, PTO requests, and commission/bonus data. Must comply with FLSA overtime rules (1.5x for hours over 40/week for non-exempt employees).

steps.title: Calculate Gross Pay and Deductions
steps.description: Apply federal income tax withholding per W-4, FICA (7.65% employee + 7.65% employer), state/local taxes, and benefits deductions (health insurance, 401k contributions, garnishments).

steps.title: Process Payroll and Direct Deposits
steps.description: Execute payroll run 2-3 business days before payday to allow ACH processing. Generate paystubs showing gross pay, all deductions, and net pay with year-to-date totals.

steps.title: Remit Payroll Taxes
steps.description: Deposit federal taxes (Form 941 deposits) semi-weekly or monthly based on deposit schedule. State taxes vary - some require next-day remittance, others monthly or quarterly.

steps.title: File Quarterly and Annual Reports
steps.description: Submit Form 941 quarterly (federal payroll taxes), state unemployment returns, and annual W-2s by January 31. Form 940 (federal unemployment) due January 31 annually.

items.title: Multi-State Withholding Complexity
items.text: Employees working remotely in different states create nexus. You must withhold based on where employee works, not where company is located. California, New York, and Massachusetts have aggressive enforcement.

items.title: State-Specific Paid Leave Programs
items.text: California, New York, New Jersey, Washington, and others have mandatory paid family leave programs with additional payroll taxes. New programs launching in Minnesota (2026), Maryland, Maine.

items.title: Misclassification Penalties
items.text: IRS treats misclassified 1099 contractors as W-2 employees retroactively. Penalties include back taxes, 20% accuracy penalty, plus potential criminal charges for willful violations.

items.title: Automate Multi-State Calculations
items.text: Use payroll software with built-in state tax tables that update automatically. Manual calculations across 50 states with different rules is error-prone and time-intensive.

items.title: FICA Wage Base Tracking
items.text: Monitor Social Security wage base ($176,100 for 2025). Once employee reaches this limit, stop withholding the 6.2% Social Security portion but continue Medicare withholding.

items.title: Year-End W-2 Preparation
items.text: Start reconciling payroll totals in November. Common errors: incorrect Box 16 (state wages), missing Box 14 items (union dues, Section 125), and wrong employer state ID numbers.

steps.title: Direct Deposit (ACH)
steps.description: Standard method (93% usage). Requires NACHA file generation. 2-day processing window typical. Same-day ACH available for urgencies ($0.50-$1.00 fee per txn).

steps.title: Paper Checks
steps.description: Still legally required option in some states. High fraud risk and manual handling cost ($3-$5 per check). Escheatment laws apply to uncashed checks.

steps.title: Pay Cards
steps.description: Debit cards for unbanked employees. Must comply with CFPB rules: employees must have free withdrawals and access to balance without fees.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss a payroll tax deposit?
faqs.answer: IRS penalties escalate rapidly: 2% (1-5 days late), 5% (6-15 days), 10% (16+ days), up to 15% after notice. Trust Fund Recovery Penalty allows IRS to seize personal assets of owners/officers for willful non-payment.

faqs.question: Can I pay employees in cryptocurrency?
faqs.answer: Yes, but complex. IRS treats crypto as property. Must value in USD at time of payment for tax withholding. Withholding must be remitted in USD. Usually easier to use hybrid crypto-payroll provider.

faqs.question: How do garnishments work?
faqs.answer: Employers must withhold court-ordered debts (child support, student loans, tax levies). Priority rules apply if multiple orders exist. Consumer Credit Protection Act limits amount (usually 25% of disposable earnings).

faqs.question: Can I run US payroll from a foreign entity?
faqs.answer: Generally no. You need a US Federal EIN and US bank account to make tax deposits. Without a US entity, you must use an Employer of Record (EOR) service.

faqs.question: What is the most common pay frequency?
faqs.answer: Bi-weekly (26 pay periods) is most common as it simplifies overtime calculations. Semi-monthly (24 periods) is popular for salaried staff. Some states (e.g., NY, CA) have strict frequency requirements for manual workers.

items.title: $80K Salary Example (California)
items.text: Gross: $6,667/month. Deductions: Federal income tax $950, Social Security $413, Medicare $97, CA state tax $380, CA SDI $67. Net pay: ~$4,760 (71% take-home). Employer costs: +$513 FICA, +$56 FUTA/SUI = Total $7,236.

items.title: State Tax Variations
items.text: No state income tax: AK, FL, NV, NH, SD, TN, TX, WA, WY. Highest: CA (13.3%), HI (11%), NY (10.9%). Same $80K salary nets $5,140/month in Texas vs $4,760 in California - $380/month difference.

steps.title: Federal & State Withholding Certificates
steps.description: Collect IRS Form W-4 and state-specific forms (e.g., CA DE-4, NY IT-2104) to determine correct withholding rates.

steps.title: Payment Method Authorization
steps.description: Secure signed direct deposit authorization forms and set up employee bank profiles in your payroll system.

steps.title: Benefit & Voluntary Deductions
steps.description: Configure pre-tax (401k, health) and post-tax deductions based on employee elections and plan documents.

faqs.question: How do I calculate hourly vs salary net pay?
faqs.answer: Salary: Annual ÷ 26 (bi-weekly) or ÷ 24 (semi-monthly). Hourly: Hours × Rate + overtime (1.5x over 40hrs/week). Both subject to same tax withholding. Use IRS Form W-4 to determine federal withholding based on filing status and dependents.

items.title: Pre-Tax vs Post-Tax
items.description: Pre-tax: 401k contributions, health insurance premiums, HSA, FSA, commuter benefits - reduce taxable income. Post-tax: Roth 401k, disability insurance, garnishments - deducted from net pay.

items.title: Maximizing Take-Home
items.description: Contribute to pre-tax 401k ($23,000 limit 2025 + $7,500 catch-up if 50+), HSA ($4,150 individual, $8,300 family), and pre-tax commuter benefits ($315/month 2025) to lower taxable income.

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions in United States
heroData.subtitle: Unified HR technology for multi-state workforce management
heroData.description: US HRIS must handle 50-state compliance, ACA reporting (1094-C/1095-C), EEO-1 filings, and integration with payroll, benefits, and time tracking systems.
heroData.bestFor: Mid-market and enterprise companies centralizing HR operations

sections.title: HRIS Implementation Process
sections.subtitle: From System Selection to Full Deployment

steps.title: Requirements Assessment
steps.description: Define must-have features: multi-state compliance, ACA reporting (1094-C/1095-C for employers with 50+ FTEs), payroll integration, time tracking, and benefits administration.

steps.title: Vendor Selection and Contracting
steps.description: Evaluate HRIS vendors on pricing ($8-$17 PEPM), SOC 2 compliance, data residency, and API capabilities. Most implementations take 3-6 months from contract signature.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Extract employee data from legacy systems, clean and validate data integrity, then import to new HRIS. Critical fields include SSN, DOB, compensation history, and benefit elections.

steps.title: Configuration and Testing
steps.description: Set up workflows for onboarding, performance reviews, and time-off requests. Configure approval hierarchies, notifications, and compliance reporting. Test payroll integration thoroughly.

items.title: ACA Reporting Deadline
items.text: Employers with 50+ full-time equivalent employees must file Forms 1094-C and 1095-C by March 31 annually. Penalties start at $310 per form for late/missing filings.

items.title: EEO-1 Filing Requirements
items.text: Companies with 100+ employees (or 50+ for federal contractors) must file EEO-1 reports annually categorizing workforce by race, ethnicity, gender, and job category.

items.title: Data Security Standards
items.text: Ensure HRIS vendor has SOC 2 Type II certification and complies with state privacy laws (California CPRA, Virginia CDPA). Employee data must be encrypted at rest and in transit.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right HRIS for multi-state compliance?
faqs.answer: Prioritize systems with automatic state tax table updates, built-in ACA tracking, and state-specific labor law posters. Verify they support all states where you have employees.

faqs.question: What is the typical cost of an HRIS?
faqs.answer: For SMBs (under 100 employees), expect $6-$15 per employee per month (PEPM). Enterprise systems (Workday, Oracle) often require annual contracts starting at $100k+. Implementation fees range from 20-50% of annual license cost.

faqs.question: Do I need an HRIS for under 10 employees?
faqs.answer: Not strictly required, but recommended if you have remote workers in different states. A simple PEO or payroll-focused HRIS (like Gusto/Rippling) can automate state tax registrations and compliance for <$100/month.

items.title: SOC 2 Compliance
items.description: Ensure HRIS vendor has SOC 2 Type II certification for handling sensitive employee data (SSNs, health info). GDPR/CCPA compliance required if storing California resident or EU employee data.

items.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
items.description: Implement SAML-based SSO (Okta, Azure AD) for secure access and centralized user management. Reduces password fatigue and improves security posture. Most modern HRIS systems support SSO integration.

heroData.title: Accounting Services in United States
heroData.subtitle: GAAP compliance and multi-state tax reporting
heroData.description: US accounting follows Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) with complex tax filing requirements across federal, state, and local jurisdictions. Public companies must comply with SEC regulations and SOX requirements.
heroData.bestFor: Businesses needing compliant financial reporting and tax preparation

steps.title: Transaction Recording
steps.description: Record all revenue, expenses, payroll, accruals. Reconcile bank accounts, credit cards, AP/AR. Use accrual accounting for businesses over $25M revenue. Close books by 5th business day of following month.

steps.title: Adjusting Entries
steps.description: Post depreciation, amortization, prepaid adjustments, accrued expenses. Review inventory valuation (FIFO, LIFO, weighted average). Match revenue with period expenses per matching principle.

steps.title: Financial Reporting
steps.description: Generate income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement. Public companies have 40-90 days to file 10-Q/10-K with SEC. Private companies report to investors/lenders monthly or quarterly.

items.title: GAAP vs IFRS
items.text: US public companies must use GAAP, not IFRS. Key differences: LIFO inventory allowed under GAAP (banned in IFRS), different revenue recognition timing, stricter R&D capitalization rules under GAAP.

items.title: SOX Compliance Costs
items.text: Sarbanes-Oxley Act applies to public companies. Section 404 internal control audits cost $1-5M annually for mid-size companies. Criminal penalties for false certifications: up to 20 years prison.

items.title: ASC 606 Revenue Recognition
items.text: New revenue standard requires 5-step model: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine price, allocate price, recognize when obligation satisfied. Impacts SaaS, construction, multi-element arrangements.

items.title: Audit (Highest Assurance)
items.description: Intensive examination of financial records, internal controls, and source documents. Opinion provided on fairness of presentation. Required for IPOs and public companies.

items.title: Review (Limited Assurance)
items.description: Consists of inquiries and analytical procedures. Less scope than audit, no internal control testing. Often accepted by banks for smaller loans.

items.title: Compilation (No Assurance)
items.description: CPA presents management's data in financial statement format without verifying accuracy. Lowest cost, used for internal use or simple tax prep.

faqs.question: When do I need a formal audit?
faqs.answer: Required for public companies (SEC rules), companies over certain revenue thresholds per state law (e.g., California Nonprofit Integrity Act), and often required by lenders or investors. Annual cost: $15K-$100K+ for private companies, $50K-$500K+ for public.

faqs.question: Cash vs Accrual Basis?
faqs.answer: Cash basis records revenue when cash received (simple, tax deferral). Accrual records when earned (GAAP required, better performance visibility). IRS requires accrual for C-Corps with >$29M gross receipts.

items.title: OSHA Workplace Safety
items.text: Occupational Safety & Health Administration fines range from $15,625 per violation (serious) to $156,259 (willful/repeated). Required: injury reporting (OSHA 300 log), hazard communication, safety training.

items.title: EEOC Anti-Discrimination
items.text: Applies to employers with 15+ employees. Prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age (40+), disability. Median settlement: $40K-$200K. Largest verdicts exceed $1M.

items.title: State Privacy Laws
items.text: CCPA/CPRA (California), Virginia CDPA, Colorado CPA create consumer data rights: access, deletion, opt-out of sale. Violations: $7,500 per intentional violation. Requires privacy policy, data mapping.

steps.title: Audit Current State
steps.description: Review employment policies, workplace safety, data protection, financial reporting. Identify gaps vs. OSHA, EEOC, DOL, FTC, state law requirements.

steps.title: Implement Controls
steps.description: Develop policies, train employees, establish reporting mechanisms. Common: compliance calendar, document retention policy (7 years for employment records), whistleblower hotline.

steps.title: Monitor and Update
steps.description: Conduct quarterly compliance reviews, track regulatory changes, update policies. Use compliance software for automated tracking and alerts.

items.title: Minimum Wage Divergence
items.text: Federal minimum wage remains $7.25/hr. States are higher: Washington ($16.66), California ($16.50), New York ($16.00). Cities can be even higher (West Hollywood $19.08). Always pay the highest applicable rate.

items.title: Paid Family Leave Patchwork
items.text: No federal mandate (FMLA is unpaid). Mandatory paid leave programs active in CA, NY, NJ, WA, MA, CO, OR, CT, RI, DE, MD, MN, ME. Funded by payroll taxes.

items.title: Pay Transparency Laws
items.text: California, New York, Washington, Colorado, and others require salary ranges in job postings. Applies to remote roles if they *could* be performed in those states.

faqs.question: What are DOL wage and hour compliance requirements?
faqs.answer: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) sets minimum wage ($7.25 federal, higher in many states), overtime (1.5x for 40+ hrs/week). Exempt employees must meet salary ($844/week in 2025) and duties tests. Misclassification penalties: back wages, liquidated damages, fines.

faqs.question: What is 'at-will' employment?
faqs.answer: Employment can be terminated by employer or employee at any time for any reason (non-discriminatory) or no reason. Standard in all states except Montana. Contracts can override this.

faqs.question: Do I need an employee handbook?
faqs.answer: Not federally required, but highly recommended as first line of defense. Must include specific policies (anti-harassment, FMLA, etc.) depending on company size and state.

items.title: R&D Tax Credit
items.description: Federal credit of 6-8% of qualified research expenses. Startups can offset $250K against payroll taxes annually. Qualified activities include software development, process improvement, engineering. Requires contemporaneous documentation.

items.title: GILTI and Subpart F
items.description: Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income (GILTI) taxes foreign earnings over 10% ROA at reduced rate. Section 250 deduction brings effective GILTI rate to 10.5% (13.125% after 2025). Critical for tech companies with foreign IP.

items.title: State Tax Nexus
items.description: Economic nexus triggers state tax filing if revenue/transactions exceed thresholds (e.g., $100K revenue or 200 transactions). Remote work creates nexus in employee home states. Failure to file incurs penalties and back taxes.

items.title: Section 199A Deduction
items.description: Pass-through entities (S-Corps, partnerships, sole proprietorships) get 20% QBI deduction. Phases out over $383K-$483K for joint filers (2025 limits). Not available for specified service businesses above threshold.

steps.title: IRS Federal EIN Registration
steps.description: Apply for Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN). Required for tax filing, payroll deposits, and opening business bank accounts.

steps.title: State Tax ID Registration
steps.description: Register with state tax departments in every state where you have physical or economic nexus for income, sales, and payroll taxes.

steps.title: Local Tax Account Setup
steps.description: Set up accounts for city or county specific taxes where applicable (e.g., NYC General Corporation Tax, Philadelphia BIRT).

items.title: Corporate Filing (Form 1120)
items.description: C-Corps: 4 months after fiscal year-end (April 15 for calendar year). S-Corps (Form 1120-S): March 15. Extensions available for 6 months (Sept 15 / Oct 15 respectively).

items.title: Quarterly Estimated Taxes
items.description: Pay if expect to owe $1,000+ in tax. Due April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Jan 15. Underpayment penalties apply if pay less than 90% of current year tax or 100% of prior year.

items.title: Transfer Pricing Compliance
items.description: Intercompany transactions (services, IP, goods) between US and foreign related parties must be at 'arm's length' prices. Documentation required to avoid penalties (20-40% of adjustment). IRS scrutiny is high.

items.title: FDII Deduction
items.description: Foreign Derived Intangible Income deduction allows US C-Corps to pay lower effective tax rate (13.125%) on income from export sales or services to foreign customers. Incentivizes keeping IP in US.

items.title: Inbound Investment (FIRPTA)
items.description: Sales of US real property interests by foreign persons subject to withholding (15%) under Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act. Exceptions apply for certain corporate stocks.

faqs.question: Should I elect S-Corp status for my LLC?
faqs.answer: S-Corp election saves self-employment tax (15.3% on profits above reasonable salary). Worth it if net profit exceeds $60K+. Requires running payroll, reasonable W-2 compensation to owner. Not available if foreign ownership or multiple share classes.

faqs.question: What triggers sales tax collection duties?
faqs.answer: Physical presence (office, inventory, employee) OR economic nexus (often $100,000 sales or 200 transactions in state). South Dakota v. Wayfair (2018) ruling allows states to tax remote sellers. Requirement applies to Software/SaaS in many states.

heroData.title: HR & Business Software in United States
heroData.subtitle: Enterprise technology stack for US operations
heroData.description: US businesses require integrated software for HR, payroll, compliance, and operations. The SaaS market offers solutions from startups to enterprises with varying pricing models and feature sets.
heroData.bestFor: Companies building modern technology infrastructure for US operations

items.title: Cloud Infrastructure
items.text: AWS dominates with 32% market share, followed by Azure (23%), Google Cloud (11%). US data residency required for regulated industries (healthcare HIPAA, financial GLBA). Average enterprise spends $1-5M annually on cloud.

items.title: SaaS Integration Ecosystem
items.text: Average company uses 110+ SaaS apps. Key integrations: Salesforce CRM, Workday HRIS, NetSuite ERP, Slack. Use APIs and iPaaS platforms (Zapier, MuleSoft) to connect systems and avoid data silos.

steps.title: Requirements Assessment
steps.description: Define must-have features: payroll processing, benefits administration, timekeeping, compliance tracking. Consider company size, growth plans, integrations needed.

steps.title: Vendor Evaluation
steps.description: Request demos from 3-5 vendors. Compare pricing, implementation timeline (typically 30-90 days), support quality, data migration assistance. Check customer reviews on G2, Capterra.

steps.title: Implementation & Training
steps.description: Migrate employee data, configure workflows, test payroll runs. Train HR staff and employees. Plan for 1-2 payroll cycles of parallel processing to verify accuracy.

items.title: Critical Security Standards
items.text: SOC 2 Type II compliance is the gold standard for SaaS vendors processing US data. NIST Cybersecurity Framework usage provides legal safe harbor in some states (e.g. Ohio, Connecticut, Utah).

items.title: Cyber Insurance
items.text: Essential for risk transfer. Premiums increasing (up 50%+ in recent years). Insurers now require MFA, immutable backups, and incident response plans as conditions for coverage.

items.title: AI Usage Policy
items.text: Companies should establish clear policies on employee use of GenAI tools (ChatGPT, etc.) to prevent IP leakage. 'Shadow AI' usage is a growing security risk.

faqs.question: Should I use QuickBooks or enterprise ERP?
faqs.answer: QuickBooks Online ($30-$200/month) suitable for <50 employees. NetSuite or SAP ($2K-$10K+/month) needed for complex operations: multi-entity, advanced reporting, inventory management, international subsidiaries. Transition typically occurs at $10-20M revenue.

faqs.question: What is an Employer of Record (EOR) software?
faqs.answer: Platforms like Deel, Remote, or Oyster combine software with legal employment. They handle payroll, taxes, and benefits for international hires without setting up a local entity. Cost is typically $599/month/employee.

faqs.question: How do I ensure data privacy compliance?
faqs.answer: Map all personal data flows. Sign Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with all vendors. Implement access controls (SSO, MFA). Conduct annual security training for employees.

heroData.title: Business Incorporation in United States
heroData.subtitle: Choose the right entity structure for tax optimization
heroData.description: US business structures include LLC, C-Corp, S-Corp, and partnerships. Choice impacts taxation (pass-through vs corporate), liability protection, fundraising ability, and compliance requirements.
heroData.bestFor: Entrepreneurs and foreign companies establishing US operations

sections.title: Entity Formation Process
sections.subtitle: From Name Reservation to EIN Assignment

steps.title: Choose Entity Type
steps.description: LLC for flexibility, C-Corp for VC funding, S-Corp for pass-through taxation. Consider state franchise taxes - Delaware popular for C-Corps, Wyoming/Nevada for LLCs.

steps.title: File Formation Documents
steps.description: Submit Articles of Incorporation (Corp) or Articles of Organization (LLC) to state Secretary of State. Costs: $50-$500 depending on state. Processing: 1-4 weeks standard, 1-3 days expedited.

steps.title: Obtain Federal EIN
steps.description: Apply for Employer Identification Number via IRS Form SS-4. Free, instant online for US-based applicants. Foreign applicants must fax/mail (4-6 weeks processing).

steps.title: Register for State Taxes
steps.description: Register for state income tax, sales tax, and employer accounts. Requirements vary - California requires $800 minimum franchise tax, Texas has franchise tax but no income tax.

items.title: Delaware C-Corp Advantage
items.text: 70% of Fortune 500 and most VC-backed startups incorporate in Delaware due to Court of Chancery, flexible corporate law, and investor familiarity. Worth the extra $300+ annual cost for serious businesses.

items.title: S-Corp Restrictions
items.text: S-Corps limited to 100 shareholders, must be US citizens/residents, one class of stock only. Not suitable for foreign ownership or VC funding. Better for small businesses with US-only ownership.

items.title: LLC Flexibility
items.text: LLCs offer pass-through taxation, flexible management, fewer formalities than corporations. Can elect S-Corp or C-Corp tax treatment. Good for small businesses, real estate, and single-member entities.

steps.title: Initial Reporting
steps.description: File Initial Statement of Information (California: 90 days) or similar initial report. Obtain business licenses (city/county level) and Seller's Permit if selling goods.

steps.title: Corporate Governance
steps.description: Adopt bylaws (Corp) or Operating Agreement (LLC). Issue stock certificates. Hold prompt organizational meeting to appoint officers and ratify formation documents. Maintain minute book.

steps.title: Registered Agent Compliance
steps.description: Maintain continuous Registered Agent service ($100-$300/year) in state of incorporation to accept legal mail. Loss of agent can lead to administrative dissolution.

faqs.question: Should I incorporate in Delaware or my home state?
faqs.answer: Delaware if seeking VC funding or planning IPO (preferred by investors, strong legal precedent). Home state if small business focused locally (avoid dual registration, simpler compliance). Consider Wyoming/Nevada for LLCs if prioritizing privacy and low fees.

faqs.question: What's the difference between C-Corp and S-Corp taxation?
faqs.answer: C-Corp: Corporate tax (21% federal) + shareholder dividend tax (double taxation). S-Corp: Pass-through to shareholders, avoiding corporate tax but subject to individual rates. S-Corp saves self-employment tax but has ownership restrictions.

faqs.question: Do I need a physical US address?
faqs.answer: You need a Registered Agent address for legal service (cannot be PO Box). For banking, you generally need a physical office address or residential address of a US officer. Virtual mailboxes are often rejected by banks.

heroData.title: Staffing & Recruitment in United States
heroData.subtitle: Navigate competitive talent markets with strategic hiring
heroData.description: US staffing connects 11 million temporary/contract workers annually. 2025 trends: automation in screening, skills-based hiring, remote work flexibility, and tighter labor markets driving competition for talent.
heroData.bestFor: Companies scaling US teams or filling specialized roles quickly

steps.title: Job Description & Posting
steps.description: Define role requirements, salary range (now required in CA, NY, CO, WA), and benefits. Post on LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor. Average time-to-fill: 36-42 days for professional roles in 2025.

steps.title: Candidate Screening
steps.description: Use ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems) with AI screening to filter resumes. 64% more placements with HR automation per Bluehorn data. Beware of AI bias - EEOC scrutinizing algorithmic hiring.

steps.title: Interviews & Assessment
steps.description: Conduct 2-4 interview rounds: phone screen, technical/case interview, culture fit, final offer. Virtual hiring now standard - 70%+ interviews conducted remotely post-2024.

steps.title: Background Check & Offer
steps.description: Criminal background check, employment verification, education confirmation. Comply with Ban the Box laws in 37 states. Offers typically include salary, equity, 401k match, health insurance.

items.title: Tight Labor Market
items.text: Unemployment at mid-4% range with 119,000 monthly payroll additions (Sept 2025 BLS data). Employers competing aggressively - average wage growth 0.8% real gain year-over-year after inflation.

items.title: Contract-to-Hire Strategy
items.text: 40% of temporary staffing in professional/managerial roles. Companies use contract workers to maintain flexibility while evaluating permanent fit. Typical conversion: 30-40% of contractors become FTEs.

items.title: Salary Transparency Laws
items.text: California, New York, Colorado, Washington require salary ranges in job postings. Non-compliance risks fines and applicant lawsuits. Transparency also applies to internal promotions in some jurisdictions.

faqs.question: What's the difference between staffing agencies and direct hiring?
faqs.answer: Staffing agencies charge 15-25% markup on hourly rates for temp workers, or 15-30% of first-year salary for direct placements. Faster than internal recruiting (5-10 days vs 6+ weeks) but higher cost. Good for urgent needs or specialized skills.

faqs.question: How do I comply with US hiring laws?
faqs.answer: Key requirements: I-9 employment eligibility verification (all hires), E-Verify (mandatory for federal contractors), background check compliance with FCRA, salary transparency where required, and avoiding discriminatory questions per EEOC (age, religion, marital status, etc.).

heroData.title: M&A Advisory in United States
heroData.subtitle: Navigate complex acquisitions and mergers
heroData.description: US M&A market remains active with technology, healthcare, and financial services leading deal volume. Advisory services cover valuation, due diligence, deal structuring, regulatory approvals, and post-merger integration.
heroData.bestFor: Companies pursuing acquisitions or preparing for sale

steps.title: Target Identification & Valuation
steps.description: Screen potential targets, conduct preliminary valuation using DCF, comparable companies, precedent transactions. Typical multiples: 3-7x EBITDA for SMBs, 10-20x+ for high-growth tech.

steps.title: Due Diligence
steps.description: Legal, financial, operational, technical DD. Review contracts, IP, litigation, compliance, financials. Identify deal-breakers and negotiation points. Duration: 30-90 days depending on complexity.

steps.title: Deal Structure & Close
steps.description: Asset purchase vs stock purchase, earnouts, seller financing, escrow. Obtain HSR clearance if transaction size triggers ($111.4M threshold 2025). Close typically 60-120 days from LOI.

items.title: HSR Filing Requirements
items.text: Hart-Scott-Rodino filing required if transaction exceeds $111.4M (2025 threshold, adjusted annually). Filing fee: $30K-$800K based on deal size. FTC/DOJ review: 30-day initial, extendable for Second Request.

items.title: Asset vs Stock Purchase
items.text: Asset purchase: Buyer avoids liabilities, gets stepped-up basis for depreciation, but requires individual asset transfers. Stock purchase: Simpler but buyer inherits all liabilities. Tax treatment differs significantly.

faqs.question: What are typical M&A advisory fees?
faqs.answer: Investment banks charge 1-5% of transaction value (Lehman Formula common: 5% first $1M, 4% next $1M, decreasing). Mid-market advisors may use success fees of $500K-$2M minimum plus 1-3% of deal value. Lawyers charge $300-$1,200/hour.

faqs.question: How long does due diligence take?
faqs.answer: Typically 30-90 days. Includes financial (quality of earnings), legal (contracts, litigation), operational, and technical diligence. Delays often caused by poor data room preparation.

faqs.question: What is a 'Quality of Earnings' (QoE) report?
faqs.answer: A financial analysis (usually by CPA firm) to validate EBITDA by removing one-time expenses/revenues. Crucial for determining final purchase price. Buyers almost always require one.

steps.title: Day 1 Plan
steps.description: Communication strategy for employees, customers, and vendors. Secure IT access and bank accounts. Announce organizational structure changes.

steps.title: Cultural Integration
steps.description: Assess cultural differences. align benefits and compensation. Address retention of key talent (retention bonuses). Culture clashes are top reason for M&A failure.

steps.title: Systems Consolidation
steps.description: Migrate ERP, CRM, and HRIS systems. unify financial reporting standards (GAAP). Rationalize duplicate vendor contracts and real estate footprint.

heroData.title: Marketing Services in United States
heroData.subtitle: Digital and traditional marketing for US market entry
heroData.description: US marketing agencies offer SEO, PPC, social media, content marketing, and brand strategy. Digital advertising dominates with Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn as primary channels. Compliance includes CAN-SPAM, CCPA/CPRA, FTC advertising guidelines.
heroData.bestFor: International brands entering US market or scaling growth

items.title: Digital Advertising Dominance
items.text: Google and Meta control 50%+ of digital ad spend. Average cost per click: $1-$2 for search ads, $0.50-$3 for social. Conversion rates average 2-5% for e-commerce, 10-15% for lead gen in B2B.

items.title: Advertising Compliance
items.text: FTC requires clear disclosure of sponsored content, truthful claims, and substantiation. Violations result in cease-and-desist orders and fines. CAN-SPAM Act governs email marketing - requires opt-out mechanism.

items.title: Localization Requirements
items.text: US market is diverse - consider regional preferences, cultural nuances, and multi-lingual capabilities for Hispanic markets. Test messaging across different segments before scaling spend.

steps.title: Market Definition
steps.description: Identify target US demographics, geographic focus (national vs regional), and buyer personas. Conduct competitor analysis on messaging and pricing.

steps.title: Channel Selection
steps.description: Select mix based on goals: Google Ads for intent capture, Meta/TikTok for brand awareness, LinkedIn for B2B. Allocate budget: 20% test, 80% proven channels.

steps.title: Creative Adaptation
steps.description: Localize assets for US English spelling, cultural references, and diversity standards. Ensure compliance with FTC disclosure rules for endorsements.

items.title: Influencer Marketing
items.text: High ROI channel. 72% of US marketers use influencers. Micro-influencers (10k-100k followers) often deliver better engagement than celebrities. B2B influencers on LinkedIn are growing rapidly.

items.title: Content Localization
items.text: US English spelling (oz vs s) and cultural references are vital. Tone should be direct, benefit-oriented, and confident. Avoid British/European idioms that may confuse US audience.

items.title: Public Relations (PR)
items.text: US market is crowded. PR agents ($5k-$20k/mo) help secure earned media (TechCrunch, WSJ). 'Pay-to-play' is common in some trade publications.

faqs.question: What's the best channel for B2B marketing in the US?
faqs.answer: LinkedIn dominates B2B with 930M+ professionals, average $5-$15 CPM. Combine with content marketing (blogs, whitepapers), SEO for organic traffic, and account-based marketing (ABM) for enterprise deals. Email marketing has highest ROI at $36-$44 per $1 spent.

faqs.question: Are trade shows worth it?
faqs.answer: Yes, for B2B. CES, SXSW, Dreamforce are massive ecosystem events. Costs are high ($50k-$200k+ for booth/travel) but face-to-face time with decision makers is invaluable.

faqs.question: How long does SEO take to work?
faqs.answer: Typically 6-12 months to see significant organic traffic growth. Requires technical optimization, high-quality content production, and link building. Competitive keywords (e.g. 'financial services') are very expensive/difficult.
